title: Heidi
author: Johanna Spyri
short_summary: Orphaned young Heidi is sent to live with her gruff but secretly kind grandfather high in the Swiss Alps, where she quickly comes to love the mountains, the goats, and her friend Peter the goatherd. Later she is taken to the city of Frankfurt to be a companion to Clara, an invalid girl who cannot walk, but Heidi grows terribly homesick for the mountains. Eventually Clara visits the Alps herself, and the fresh air, goat's milk, and Heidi's warm friendship help her grow stronger, until she is finally able to walk again.
extended_summary:
After her parents' deaths, young Heidi is brought by her aunt to live with her grandfather, a solitary old man who lives alone in a cabin high in the Swiss Alps and has a reputation in the village for being harsh and unfriendly. Despite his gruffness, Heidi's grandfather grows to love her, and Heidi herself falls in love with life on the mountain — the fresh air, the wildflowers, and the goats she helps tend with her new friend, the goatherd boy Peter. For a few happy years, Heidi lives simply and joyfully among the mountains she comes to call home.

Heidi's aunt later takes her to Frankfurt to live with a wealthy family and be a companion to Clara, a kind girl who cannot walk and uses a wheelchair. Though Heidi and Clara become close friends, Heidi grows increasingly homesick for her grandfather, the mountains, and Peter, and eventually falls ill from longing for home, so she is sent back to the Alps. When Clara later visits Heidi in the mountains, the clean air, the goat's milk, and the joyful, active life there — along with Heidi's steady friendship and encouragement — slowly restore Clara's strength, and by the end of her visit she is able to stand and walk on her own for the first time.
